title: Oncall timeline synchronizer with trace debounce and automatic runbook links
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a synchronized oncall timeline feature that automatically attaches enriched trace context and curated runbook links to PagerDuty incidents and Slack alert threads. Goal is to reduce time-to-ack and time-to-resolution by delivering immediately actionable context: trace id, top 3 slow spans, request sample, and a deterministic runbook link based on service & error class. System will debounce noisy alerts and attach a single consolidated context blob per incident/streak.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents for runtime latency/error alerts include a link to the trace viewer with trace id prepopulated and a compact summary of the top 3 spans (service, op, ms)
Slack alert threads created from the alert pipeline show a single synchronized context message (no duplicate attachments) for a 5-minute alert window
Runbook link resolver returns a deterministic URL for a given service+error hash and is included in PD/Slack attachments
Configurable debounce window (default 5m) available in feature flags and Console with metrics visible in the incidents dashboard
End-to-end tests for trace attachment, runbook resolution, and debounce behavior in CI; unit tests for resolver and PD payload builder
Observability metrics: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) decreases by 20% for impacted services in the canary group; attachment success rate >= 95%
Feature rollout gated behind feature-flag and opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers
technical_notes: Add trace enrichment hook inside telemetry-router service: when an alert matches latency/error threshold, attach trace_id and top spans from trace-store using deterministic sampling (sampling key: alert.signature + service)
Implement a debounce coordinator in alert-manager that groups alerts by fingerprint for a configurable window (default 5m) and emits a single attachment event per group

PagerDuty integration: extend /v2/incidents payload with 'html_body' enrichment and an attachments array containing trace_link and runbook_link. Use existing PD service client (repo: infra/pagerduty-client) and add tests for rate-limits and retries
Slack integration: send a rich block message into the alert channel and pin the consolidated context. Use slack-bot token with scoped scope 'chat:write' and 'pins:write'

Runbook resolver: new microservice (repo: observability/runbook-resolver) with a small cache; mapping rules stored in Console (UI) and exposed via API. Fallback sequence: service-level runbook -> team-level -> generic 'latency-troubleshooting'
Security: trace links contain signed short-lived tokens (JWT) valid for 1 hour; ensure tokens respect VPC/private deployment rules and do not leak full payloads for Private customers
Telemetry: new metrics: incident.context_attachment.latency, incident.context_attachment.success, incident.debounce.group_size; emit tags: service, env, tier
Rollout: start with internal canary on staging -> 10% of production traffic -> 100%; monitor MTTA, PD attachment error rate, and Slack rate-limit errors. Auto-disable if errors > 5% or MTTA regresses
rollout_plan: Week 1: backend hooks + runbook-resolver prototype deployed to staging (internal)
Week 2: PD/Slack payload builders + unit tests; feature flag off by default in production
Week 3: Canary in prod (10%) with close ops monitoring and a dedicated PagerDuty channel for test incidents
Week 4: expand to 50% and begin Dedicated customer opt-in; collect MTTA/MTTR metrics
Week 5: full rollout and console toggle + docs + runbook authoring guide
